Robotic Prosthetic Market reached US$ 1.63 Billion in 2024 and is expected to reach US$ 3.16 Billion by 2033, growing at a CAGR of 7.7% during the forecast period 2025-2033.
The Robotic Prosthetic Market involves advanced prosthetic limbs integrated with robotics and smart technologies for improved mobility, dexterity, and functionality.
These devices leverage sensors, AI, and actuators to provide natural movement and user control.
Market expansion is supported by increasing limb amputations, technological advancements, and rising patient preference for personalized prosthetics.
Rehabilitation centers, hospitals, and clinics are major end-users.
The market also benefits from government support and research funding for assistive technologies.
✅ In April 2025, Phantom Neuro raised $19 million in Series A to advance its under-skin wristband device which decodes nerve signals to control prosthetic limbs.
The "Phantom X" showed ~94% accuracy across 11 hand/wrist movements.
The company is targeting arms first, then legs, with strong backing from major medtech players.
✅ In September 2025, the U.S. Department of Defense committed a $300,000 investment through DARPA's Commercial Strategy Office into Phantom Neuro.
The implantable neurotech device captures muscle electrical signals and uses AI to control prosthetic limbs.
Human testing is expected by late 2025 or early 2026 under FDA fast-track designations.
✅ In January 2025, BionicM launched its U.S. headquarters near Washington, D.C. and unveiled the Bio Leg® microprocessor-powered knee, which won a CES 2025 "Best of Innovation" award.
The expansion improves delivery lead times and after-sales service for its prosthetic solutions in the U.S. market.
✅ In March 2025, a research team at the University of Tokyo and Waseda University developed a biohybrid robot hand made using cultivated human muscle tissues.
The hand can independently move fingers and perform grasping motions, representing progress toward more human-like prosthetic hands.
✅ In May 2025, Osaka-based startup Kawatek introduced the AI-powered prosthetic hand RYO, which automatically learns and adapts to user motion.
RYO can replicate up to ~95% of hand movements and includes health-monitoring features, with commercial launch expected by late 2025 or early 2026.
✅ In March 2025, UTokyo Innovation Platform invested in Instalimb Inc., a Tokyo medtech startup using 3D printing and AI to create affordable prosthetics.
Instalimb operates in Japan, India, and the Philippines, focusing on accessibility, comfort, and cost reduction in prosthetic limb solutions.

The robotic prosthetic market is expanding due to the increasing incidence of limb loss from trauma, diabetes, and vascular disorders, as well as rising awareness of advanced rehabilitation technologies.
Innovations in sensor-based prosthetics and myoelectric systems are improving functional outcomes for users.
Key trends include integration with AI and machine learning to enable adaptive movement, lightweight materials for enhanced comfort, and customizable designs tailored to individual patients.
Collaboration with rehabilitation centers is also promoting adoption and user training.
